job: My mother lives alone and can't bend down any more. The TV remote is on the low footstool by her bed and there is a towel on the edge of the bath, please pick both up. Fetch her pill organiser from the kitchen counter and wipe her bedside table.

world.source: hand-written scenario, not a scan: a one-bedroom apartment for an older resident, with a narrow bathroom door

output.understood_as: From your mother's home, the robot should wipe her bedside table, pick up the TV remote from the low footstool and the towel from the bath edge, and bring her pill organiser from the kitchen counter.
steps: Wipe the top of the bedside table with a cloth.
Pick up the TV remote from the low footstool by the bed.
Go to the bathroom and pick up the towel from the edge of the bath.
Go to the kitchen and pick up the pill organiser from the counter to bring it to her.

tasks.why: She asked for the bedside table to be wiped; doing it first leaves a clean surface for her things.
The remote is on a low footstool she can no longer reach; it should end up somewhere she can reach.
The towel is on the low bath edge and she cannot bend down to get it.
She asked for the pill organiser to be fetched from the kitchen counter and brought to her.

demos.why: Shows the stroke pattern and pressure for wiping the bedside table top.
Shows how firmly to hold the cloth so it does not slip out while pressing on the table.
Shows how a hand reaches down to the footstool and lifts the remote.
The remote is smooth and can slip, and pressing too hard could push its buttons.
Shows how to gather and lift the towel off the bath edge without it falling into the bath.
A soft towel can slide out of a light grip, so the right grip force must be recorded.
Shows how to lift the organiser off the counter and keep it level.
Squeezing too hard can pop the lids open and spill the pills, too lightly and it slips.

questions: Where should the remote and the pill organiser end up? The robot can pick things up, but it has no 'put down' skill and no marked spot (for example her bedside table or her hand) to deliver them to. Please tell us the spot and we will add it.
What should happen to the towel once it is picked up: hung on a rail, put in a laundry basket, or handed to her? None of these places has been located yet.
The only towel card we have describes a hand towel bunched on the floor. If the towel on the bath edge is a large bath towel, please tell us roughly how heavy it is.
Where is the wiping cloth kept, and should it be dry or damp? Nobody has located it in the home yet.
